content: The nicotine patch is a transdermal delivery system approved by the FDA for managing withdrawal symptoms, including nicotine cravings, associated with smoking cessation. It is designed to provide a controlled release of nicotine through the skin to help individuals quit smoking. Contraindications and Warnings: Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should only use the nicotine patch under the guidance of a healthcare provider. Smoking during pregnancy can harm the child, and while the patch is considered safer than smoking, its risks to the child are not fully understood. The patch should not be used if the individual continues to smoke, chew tobacco, use snuff, nicotine gum, or other nicotine-containing products. Consult a doctor before use if you have heart disease, a recent heart attack, or an irregular heartbeat, as nicotine can increase heart rate. Those with adhesive tape allergies or skin problems may experience rashes and should consult a healthcare provider before use. If you are using a non-nicotine smoking cessation drug or taking prescription medications for depression or asthma, consult a doctor or pharmacist, as dosage adjustments may be necessary. Usage Instructions: Do not smoke while using the patch, even if it is not currently on your skin, as nicotine from the patch continues to enter the bloodstream for several hours after removal. If vivid dreams or sleep disturbances occur, the patch can be removed at bedtime and replaced in the morning. Stop using the patch and consult a doctor if skin redness persists beyond four days, if swelling or a rash develops, or if symptoms of nicotine overdose occur, such as nausea, vomiting, dizziness, weakness, or rapid heartbeat. Administration Guidelines: Apply one new patch every 24 hours to clean, dry, and hairless skin. Avoid using the same skin site consecutively; rotate application sites daily. After applying or removing the patch, wash your hands thoroughly. Dispose of used patches by folding the sticky sides together and placing them in the original pouch. Do not wear more than one patch at a time, and do not cut the patch into smaller pieces. Remove the patch before undergoing MRI procedures to avoid burns. The patch should not be worn for more than 24 hours, as it may cause skin irritation and lose effectiveness. Special Populations: There is no specific FDA guidance on the use of nicotine patches in pediatric, geriatric, pregnant, or nursing populations, nor in individuals with renal or hepatic impairment, immunocompromised states, or specific gender or racial groups. Storage: Store the patches at a controlled room temperature of 20-25°C (68-77°F). Counseling Points: Individuals under 18 years of age should consult a doctor before using the patch. Smoking cessation should begin completely when starting the patch. Follow the recommended schedule based on the number of cigarettes smoked daily. If smoking more than 10 cigarettes per day, follow the step-down schedule provided in the product instructions. If smoking 10 or fewer cigarettes per day, begin with Step 2 for six weeks, followed by Step 3 for two weeks, and then discontinue use. If the need to use the patch persists beyond eight weeks, consult a healthcare provider. Alcohol Interaction: The interaction between alcohol and the nicotine patch has not been established. Consult a healthcare provider regarding the use of alcohol while using this product. Overdose: In the event of suspected overdose or poisoning, contact the National Poison Help hotline at 1-800-222-1222 immediately. Additional Notes: The patch should not be used beyond the recommended duration without consulting a healthcare provider. There is limited information available regarding the pharmacology, pharmacokinetics, and clinical studies of the nicotine patch in the drug label.
